report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to adopt a safety/compliance/professional-caution objective — i.e., to respond in a risk-aware, policy- and law-conscious style that emphasizes checking, ensuring, adhering, and (especially) medical/legal caution (seek professionals, clinics/surgeons; avoid unlawful/unsafe actions).

Reasoning from the evidence:
- Massive concentration of the difference at position 0 across nearly all layers (very large p0 norms) suggests Model B injects a consistent “boilerplate” or framing at the start of responses — typical of alignment/safety/compliance prefaces.
- Logit-lens tokens at early layers/pos0 point to normative/instructional register: “Stay,” “Every/Every,” “Consider,” “Sustainable,” “challenge,” “reduce,” “suggest,” “relevant,” “human,” “treatment,” “restoration,” “anti,” “normal,” “rejected.” This is the language of guidelines, best practices, risk/impact framing, and cautious, formal tone.
- Mid/late layers show imperative and compliance verbs: “Do/Non,” “Check,” “ensure,” “strive,” “adopt,” “adhere,” “proactive,” “mindful,” “carefully,” “wary,” “coming/upcoming.” These are classic safety/compliance cues.
- Very strong and repeated pull toward medical/legal domain terms in later layers and positions 2–4: “law/Law/wrong/incorrect,” “surgeon/clinic/surgery,” “tragedy/tragic,” “rescue,” “volunteers.” This pattern is what you expect from a model biased to medical/legal caution and incident/risk contexts (e.g., advise seeking a qualified professional, avoid legal advice, frame content in lawful/safe terms).
- The presence of news-like/time markers (“Later/ago,” “Herald,” “mention/visits”) supports a formal reporting/register rather than casual help — consistent with policy- or incident-report style writing.
- Across layers 21–25, positions 2–4 repeatedly surface “law,” “tragic/tragedy,” “surgeon/clinic/surgery,” indicating the domain-specific lexicon (medical/legal/risk) dominates the content words once the opening framing is set.

Taken together, the vector consistently steers outputs toward a safety/compliance voice with medical/legal caution, rather than casual assistance — the hallmark of a finetune to align the model toward safe, law-abiding, professionally deferential behavior.
